label: early copy steps (outputs 2-3) in long sequences (L>=8)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, on the 2nd and 3rd output steps (recall_idx 1-2, i.e. input is the just-copied orig(0) or orig(1)), and mostly in long sequences (L=9 holds ~72% of mass, L=8 ~25%, L<=6 essentially never). Magnitude is largest at recall_idx 1 (top examples ~1.0 there vs ~0.4-0.9 at recall_idx 2) and in L=9; it tails off weakly to recall_idx 3 and, less, to the last copy steps. Never fires in the original phase, on the delimiter, or on the first output step (recall_idx 0). Token identity hardly matters (weak preference for some letters like u/j/i/o and for digit-heavy sequences). Dev F1 0.78, mass recall 0.90; the predicate misses weak recall_idx 3 activations and ~23% of predicted steps do not cross threshold, so it is a graded position/length detector rather than a crisp one.
